heard: Undocking to escape a violent spin made Armstrong's capsule spin faster. Most people assume separating from a target vehicle instantly solves a docking emergency. On March 16, 1966, astronauts Neil Armstrong and David Scott launched on the Gemini 8 mission. After completing the first United States space docking, a thruster short-circuited and stuck open. Thinking the target caused the spin, they undocked, which made the lighter capsule spin even faster. The uncontrolled rotation accelerated, reaching nearly one revolution per second and threatening a blackout. Using 75% of their emergency fuel, Armstrong stabilized the ship for immediate abort. They only survived because they realized why.
